newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX dips before U.S. data, mid-caps shine.
newsitem.headline: German DAX dips before U.S. data, mid-caps shine.

text.p: Uncertainty ahead of the release of December price data from the U.S. kept the German share market muted on Tuesday, with the blue chip DAX index sliding slightly although mid-cap stocks outperformed.
The 30-share DAX closed the bourse session down 6.07 points at 2,948.88 as the market awaited the U.S. report at 1330 GMT.
"People feel it's time for a breather now. Who knows what could happen this afternoon?," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"I think 3,000 is still a goal (for the DAX) but I don't see us taking a run at it today," he added.
March DTB DAX futures were down 6.5 points at 2,967.5.
Mid-cap stocks fared well, however, with the recently launched MDAX mid-cap index ending up 6.48 points at a record high close of 3,081.80.

The main excitement of the day broke minutes into bourse dealings when the government announced a new draft airline law which should force Deutsche Lufthansa AG to convert its stock to unpopular non-freely transferable shares.
Blue chip Lufthansa shares plunged as much as five percent to 20.60 marks on the news, before calming to close at 21.01 marks, down 84 pfennigs.

Analysts called the drop exaggerated but dealers said investors, especially foreign investors, were worried that their rights might be restricted and the fact that Lufthansa said it had not reached a decision on a rights issue.
"The whole deal is making people less sure of the company," said one trader.

Chemicals group Hoechst AG also came under some pressure after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposed withdrawing its approval for its allergy drug Seldane because a safer alternative was available.
Hoechst ended off its lows. however, down 25 pfennigs at 69.85 marks.
